Prevention: Proper drainage conditions in the field should be maintained by raised bed planting.
Select sites with good air movement and provide adequate spacing between plants to allow air movement.
Plant crops earlier in the spring (late
Avoiding overhead irrigation to prevent leaf wetness.
Control alternate weed hosts (wild cucumber ) in neighbouring fence rows and field edges.
Apply recommended dose of urea, DAP and
MOP for better soil fertility and crop growth.
Consider rotation using non- cucurbits crops such as okra and brinjal.
Monitoring: Monitor the field at weekly intervals starting from the vegetative to fruiting stages.
Fungal development is most noticable during humid conditions (early mornings and following rainfall) on the underside of leaves.
Some symtoms are more visible when leaves are wet.
Yellow spots of downy mildew, on the upper surface of a leaf; they are often angular and restricted by the leaf veins.
Look to see the purple-grey, downy or felt-like growth on the underside of the leaves where the spores form.
August and is more serious during the mid and later parts of the rainy season.
Severe infections results in necrosis of leaves and wilting.
Direct Control: Removal and destruction of highly infected lower leaves.
Restrict the movement of water from infested areas to healthy areas.
